sections.name: Priced as services. Size moves your number more than the label does.

items.text: Priced as services. Size moves your number more than the label does.

Services businesses are bought on earnings, and the multiple rises with size. One survey puts services within a turn of information technology at the same size. A transaction database puts them more than ten turns apart. We do not know which is right, and we will not pick one silently.

sections.name: Six lines a buyer recomputes from your own records.

items.text: Services · What a buyer reads first
Six lines a buyer recomputes from your own records.
Services businesses are bought on adjusted earnings, and the multiple rises with size. What a buyer reads is how durable the earnings are once the owner steps back.
What repeats, and under what paper
Retainers, managed services and maintenance contracts are read apart from projects. A buyer prices the repeating part on one multiple and the project part on another.
Labor is the cost of revenue. A buyer rebuilds utilization and realization by person and by month, and reads the trend before the average.
Signed work with a start date is backlog. Everything else is pipeline. A buyer counts only the first and asks how the second converted last year.
The five largest customers, and where the next ones come from. A services business whose work arrives through one referral source has a concentration a buyer will find.
Unbilled work is an asset a buyer discounts. Overbilling is a liability a buyer counts as debt-like. Both come out of the working capital target.
Who sells, who delivers, who decides
If the owner sells the work and delivers the hardest of it, the buyer prices the transition: a longer consulting term, an earnout, or a lower number.

sections.name: As owners keep it. As a buyer reads it.

items.text: Services · How the numbers are read
As owners keep it. As a buyer reads it.
Recurring and project revenue apart, each with its own margin, recognized when earned rather than when billed.
Cost of revenue by person and by engagement, with utilization and realization by month and the subcontractor share.
Realized rates against the card, discounts by customer, and the share of fixed-fee work that ran over budget.
Concentration, contract terms, renewal dates, and the referral sources behind the new ones.
Receivables aging, unbilled work, overbillings and payables on a monthly trend; a target set from the trailing twelve months.
Owner compensation normalized to a market salary, and the owner’s own billable hours priced as a cost of replacing them.

sections.name: Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.

items.text: Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.
Why are the published multiples so far apart?

Because they measure different things. A banker survey reports recast earnings multiples by size band; a transaction database reports what closed. The pages show both and do not reconcile them. Your own number depends on size, contracts and what the earnings are once traced to source.
Does recurring revenue change how a services business is priced?
Yes, where it is contracted and reported apart. A retainer with a term is priced differently from a project that may repeat.
What does a buyer do about my own hours?

Prices them. If you sell the work and deliver the hardest of it, the buyer prices the transition. The review shows how much of the business runs through you, so you can change it before a buyer measures it.
Will the review raise my price?
We will not promise that. It shows what your numbers support and gives you the chance to fix what they do not before a buyer prices it.
You. Nothing reaches a buyer, an adviser or anyone else without your written permission.
